items.answer: Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

The systemic definition of augmented reality (AR) states that an AR system should have three characteristics: combining the real world with virtual content, being interactive in real time so that interaction with the digital content added to the real-world view is reflected immediately, and being registered in 3D.

The formative years of virtual reality are the second phase of its historical evolution, roughly 1950 to 1990 after computers appeared in the 1940s, beginning with development of head-mounted displays (HMDs) in the 1950s and ending with popularization of the term virtual reality in the late 1980s.

questions.question: How do the historical phases of augmented reality differ from the phases of virtual reality?
options: The AR phases may sometimes overlap
The AR phases are strictly sequential
Neither the AR phases nor the VR phases may overlap
The VR phases may sometimes overlap
questions.explanation: The AR historical phases are described as phases that may sometimes overlap, unlike the phases of virtual reality.

questions.question: Which phase of augmented reality involved early experimentation that defined concepts and showed the types of technology required for AR?
options: The basic research phase
The commercial application phase
The experimental phase
The tools or applications phase
questions.explanation: The experimental phase is characterized as involving early experimentation that defined AR concepts and showed the types of technology required.

questions.question: What was the main focus of the basic research phase of augmented reality?
options: Early experimentation that defined concepts and required technology types
Developing or exploring early applications and usability of such applications
Research into enabling technologies such as tracking, displays, and input devices
Widespread AR availability and newer applications in several domains
questions.explanation: The basic research phase involved research into enabling technologies, including tracking, displays, and input devices.

questions.question: Which phase of augmented reality was associated with widespread availability and newer applications?
options: The commercial application phase
The experimental phase
The tools or applications phase
The basic research phase
questions.explanation: The commercial application phase involved widespread AR availability and newer applications appearing in various domains.

data.text: The historical evolution of augmented reality can be broadly divided into four overlapping phases from before the 1980s to the present. These phases progressed from early experimentation and basic research into the development of tools and widespread commercial applications.
points: The historical evolution of augmented reality can be broadly divided into four overlapping phases from before the 1980s to the present.
These phases progressed from early experimentation and basic research into the development of tools and widespread commercial applications.

questions.question: Which display type was part of the first computer-generated AR prototype?
options: An LCD-based see-through hand-held display
A CRT-based optical see-through head-mounted display
A CRT-based fully immersive head-mounted display
A projection-based desktop see-through display
questions.explanation: The first Sutherland-Sproull AR prototype combined a CRT-based optical see-through head-mounted display with a ceiling-mounted tracking system.

questions.question: What did the tracking system in the first computer-generated AR prototype register?
options: Eye movements in a virtual display
Hand movements in two dimensions on a hand-held display
Body orientation in an aircraft cockpit
Head movements in three dimensions on the see-through display
questions.explanation: The mechanical tracking system registered head movements in three dimensions on the see-through display.

questions.question: In the super cockpit prototype, when was the real-world view replaced by computer-generated imagery?
options: During daylight
Only when the aircraft was on the ground
Only during takeoff and landing
At night or in bad weather
questions.explanation: In daylight, computer-generated imagery was superimposed over the real-world view; at night or in bad weather, it replaced the real-world view.

questions.question: Which hardware category was an outcome of early AR experiments?
options: Shared multi-user AR room systems
Projection-based desktop AR displays
Hand-held mobile AR displays
Input and tracking hardware
questions.explanation: Early AR experiments led to head-mounted AR displays used in modern aircraft, VR displays such as the VIVED HMD, and input and tracking hardware.

data.text: Ivan Sutherland and Bob Sproull created the first computer-generated augmented reality prototype in 1968. This prototype used a head-mounted display and a tracking system to register head movements in three dimensions. The US Air Force super cockpit program produced technologies where pilots saw computer-generated imagery through a head-mounted display. These early experiments led to modern aircraft displays, virtual reality systems, and tracking hardware.
points: Ivan Sutherland and Bob Sproull created the first computer-generated augmented reality prototype in 1968.
This prototype used a head-mounted display and a tracking system to register head movements in three dimensions.
The US Air Force super cockpit program produced technologies where pilots saw computer-generated imagery through a head-mounted display.
These early experiments led to modern aircraft displays, virtual reality systems, and tracking hardware.

questions.question: What characterized the basic research phase of augmented reality?
options: Mid-1990s shared augmented workspaces
Medical image-guided surgery applications
Influential 1990s research that shaped the field
Outdoor wearable GPS navigation applications
questions.explanation: The basic research phase came after the experimentation phase and included influential 1990s work that shaped augmented reality.

questions.question: What type of display did University of North Carolina augmented-reality research investigate as typically used in augmented reality?
options: Stereoscopic video displays
Outdoor GPS-based interfaces
See-through head-mounted displays
Handheld liquid-crystal displays
questions.explanation: University of North Carolina research during the basic research phase included early work on see-through head-mounted displays, which are typically used in augmented reality.

questions.question: How did Chameleon present virtual content to a user?
options: By superimposing virtual tags on real objects
By using GPS to locate outdoor markers
By overlaying virtual cues on stereoscopic video
By moving an LCD over paper
questions.explanation: Chameleon allowed a user to move a liquid-crystal display over a piece of paper and see virtual content, making it an early handheld or mobile augmented-reality system.

questions.question: What did NaviCam superimpose on real objects?
options: Virtual tags
Shared augmented content
Outdoor navigation information
Virtual cues
questions.explanation: NaviCam was a handheld or mobile augmented-reality system that superimposed virtual tags on real objects using handheld and head-mounted displays.

questions.question: What is often credited with introducing the term augmented reality into academic work?
options: The first handheld AR system
The first see-through head-mounted display
The first academic article containing the term
The first mobile AR publication
questions.explanation: Tom Caudell is often credited with coining the phrase augmented reality because he published the first academic article containing the term AR.

data.text: The basic research phase of augmented reality came after the experimentation phase and shaped the field during the 1990s, including the coining of the term "augmented reality" in 1992. Research during this phase focused on tracking techniques, head-mounted displays, and interaction methods. Early systems like Chameleon and NaviCam were true augmented reality applications and precursors to the kind of AR applications seen today.
points: The basic research phase of augmented reality came after the experimentation phase and shaped the field during the 1990s.
Tom Caudell coined the term "augmented reality" in 1992.
Research during this phase focused on tracking techniques, head-mounted displays, and interaction methods.
Early systems like Chameleon and NaviCam were true augmented reality applications and precursors to the kind of AR applications seen today.

questions.question: What capability did some augmented reality systems developed in the mid-1990s give to people in the same location?
options: They allowed those people to see and interact with shared augmented reality content.
They allowed those people to replace the real location with a projected virtual location.
They allowed those people to move entirely into a shared virtual room.
They allowed those people to interact with separate augmented images from separate rooms.
questions.explanation: Mid-1990s AR work included systems that let people in the same location see and interact with shared augmented reality content.

questions.question: Which medical applications were developed during the mid-1990s tools or applications phase of augmented reality?
options: X-ray visualization in a patient's body, full virtual surgery simulation, and wearable navigation games
Visualization of laparoscopic surgery, remote robotic surgery, and drug-dosing alerts
Image-guided surgery, video conferencing with surgeons, and marker-based outdoor navigation
Visualization of laparoscopic surgery, X-ray visualization in a patient's body, and image-guided surgery.
questions.explanation: Medical AR applications from that phase included visualization of laparoscopic surgery, X-ray visualization in a patient's body, and image-guided surgery.

questions.question: Why was viewpoint tracking a significant challenge in augmented reality?
options: It had to be addressed so that virtual rooms could replace real environments completely.
It had to be addressed so that three-dimensional registration of content could happen accurately.
It had to be addressed so that shared AR content could be displayed on separate screens.
It had to be addressed so that users could hear immersive audio more clearly.
questions.explanation: Viewpoint tracking was significant because it enabled accurate three-dimensional registration of AR content.

questions.question: What did the AR Toolkit tracking library provide for augmented reality systems?
options: Real-time GPS positioning for outdoor navigation
Real-time rendering of fully virtual environments
Real-time generation of immersive audio for head-mounted displays
Real-time computer-vision tracking of a square marker, helping track a user's viewpoint.
questions.explanation: The AR Toolkit provided real-time computer-vision tracking of a square marker, which could help an AR system track a user's viewpoint.

questions.question: What applications were included in outdoor wearable augmented reality during the tools or applications phase?
options: Aerial navigation, remote viewing and deletion of computer-aided design models, and web-based shopping
Terrestrial navigation, on-site viewing and creation of computer-aided design models, and game playing.
Indoor navigation, on-site viewing and creation of computer-aided design models, and virtual reality gaming
Terrestrial navigation, remote viewing and creation of computer-aided design models, and social networking
questions.explanation: Outdoor wearable AR applications included terrestrial navigation, on-site viewing and creation of computer-aided design models, and game playing.

data.text: Research in the mid-1990s focused on key technologies like tracking, display, and interaction, leading to developments in shared AR content, medical applications, and wearable computing. By 1997, computer vision and GPS were used to register 3D content in the real world. In the early 2000s, wearable AR systems were developed for various applications but remained bulky and difficult to use. Viewpoint tracking challenges were eventually addressed by systems like the AR Toolkit, which was later ported to mobile phones in 2004.
points: Mid-1990s research focused on key enabling technologies like tracking, display, and interaction.
This period saw the development of shared AR content, medical applications, and wearable computing using head-mounted displays.
By 1997, tracking techniques using computer vision markers and GPS were used to register 3D content.
In the early 2000s, wearable AR systems were developed for various applications but were bulky and difficult to use.
Viewpoint tracking was addressed by tools such as the AR Toolkit, which was later ported to mobile phones in 2004.

questions.question: What marked the beginning of the commercial application phase of augmented reality?
options: A laboratory-only AR tool became widely adopted
An outdoor GPS-based wearable AR interface was first shown
A widely used consumer AR experience became available
An open-source marker tracking library was released
questions.explanation: The segment says the commercial application phase began when a widely used consumer AR experience was released, after AR had been neither very popular nor easily available.

questions.question: What factors helped augmented reality move from research laboratories and specialist applications to widely available commercial technology?
options: Web-browser AR authoring, smartphone-based AR, and global marketing campaigns
Backpack computers, HMD displays, and GPS outdoor navigation
Virtual reality headsets, haptic feedback, and metaverse platforms
Computer-vision marker tracking, shared AR content, and image-guided surgery
questions.explanation: AR became widely available because AR authoring tools made web-browser AR possible, smartphones had become common, and global marketing campaigns used AR to promote products.

questions.question: What did the launch of AR development platforms for major mobile platforms help achieve?
options: AR development required only custom computer hardware in a backpack
Only simple AR applications could be created
Many developers could create AR applications, increasing apps from simple to complex ones
AR was restricted to specialist research laboratories
questions.explanation: These development platforms further stimulated AR growth by enabling many developers to create AR applications and by increasing the number of AR applications from simple to complex ones.

questions.question: Which developments are expected to support continued growth of the AR commercial application phase?
options: Better AI and computer vision that make 3D tracking feasible only on high-end devices
More AR applications and tools, hardware improvements, and better algorithms, AI, and computer vision for 3D tracking on low-end devices
Only more marker-based AR applications and bulky wearable computers
More complex AR applications, but without hardware or tracking improvements
questions.explanation: The segment says the phase is expected to keep growing through more applications and tools, improved wearable, mobile, and holographic hardware, and better algorithms, AI, and computer vision that make 3D tracking and registration more feasible on low-end devices.

data.text: The commercial application phase of augmented reality began in October 2007 and moved from research laboratories to widely available technology by 2009, driven by new authoring tools, smartphones, and marketing campaigns. The launch of ARKit and ARCore in 2017 further stimulated growth by enabling developers to create complex applications. This phase is expected to continue growing as hardware improves and AI and computer vision technologies advance.
points: The commercial application phase of augmented reality began in October 2007 and made the technology popular among consumers.
In 2009, augmented reality moved from research laboratories to widely available commercial technology.
This shift was driven by Adobe Flash-based authoring tools, the start of the smartphone era, and global marketing campaigns.
The launch of ARKit and ARCore in 2017 stimulated growth by enabling developers to create more complex applications.
The commercial application phase is still ongoing and is expected to continue growing through improvements in hardware, AI, and computer vision.

questions.question: How does the historical framing of augmented reality differ from the historical framing of virtual reality's formative years?
questions.reference_answer: The formative years of virtual reality are described as roughly 1950 to 1990, ending with the popularization of the term virtual reality in the late 1980s. In contrast, the historical evolution of augmented reality is divided into four phases that may sometimes overlap. Those AR phases are the experimental phase before the 1980s, the basic research phase from the 1980s to the mid-1990s, the tools or applications phase from the mid-1990s to 2007, and the commercial application phase from 2007 to the present.

questions.question: What does the Sutherland-Sproull prototype show about how an early augmented reality system could satisfy the systemic requirements of combining real and virtual content and being registered in 3D?
questions.reference_answer: Ivan Sutherland and Bob Sproull created the first truly computer-generated augmented reality prototype in 1968, using a CRT-based optical see-through head-mounted display and a ceiling-mounted mechanical tracking system connected to a PDP-11 computer and custom graphics hardware. The tracker registered head movements in three dimensions on the see-through display. The systemic definition of an augmented reality system says that it combines the real world with virtual content and is registered in 3D, and the prototype's see-through HMD with 3D head registration corresponds to those characteristics.

questions.question: What connection can be drawn between early handheld augmented reality systems such as NaviCam and the later commercial growth of mobile augmented reality?
questions.reference_answer: NaviCam was a 1995 handheld or mobile augmented reality system that superimposed virtual tags on real objects using handheld and head-mounted displays. Early handheld systems like NaviCam were true augmented reality applications and precursors to the kind of AR applications seen today. In 2009, augmented reality moved to widely available commercial technology partly because of smartphone-based augmented reality, and Apple's ARKit and Google's ARCore further stimulated growth by enabling many developers to create augmented reality applications.
